text: /// The packages whose plugins the user has enabled, to load at sync time.
/// 1. workspace **dependencies** covered by `[plugins] auto-enable` or an
/// 2. packages named by a `use` entry that are **not** dependencies:
///    `cargo agents use <crate>` pulls a plugin in from crates.io whether or
///    not the workspace depends on it.
/// `auto-enable` intentionally contributes only (1): it is consent for what a
/// dependency you already have carries, not a way to add crates. Declined
/// packages are pruned. A `use` name is resolved through the package managers
/// ([`PmRegistry::identify`]) at `update`: one that names a plugin in
/// `registry` is left out, since that plugin is loaded already and
/// [`used_plugins`] wakes it, and one that no package manager has is skipped.
let used = resolve_used(sym, pms, registry, workspace_root, update).await;
for id in dep_ids.iter().filter(|id| id.pm == CARGO_PM) {
/// Classify one offer against the `[plugins]` config. `disable` outranks every
/// other entry, and an explicit `use` outranks the standing `auto-enable`, so a
/// name the user declined stays declined.
// `disable` is tested first because it is the last word: every other
// entry says a plugin *may* run, and this is the only one that says it
// may not. Activation agrees (see `record_active`), so classifying a
// disabled plugin as `Used` here would report it active while it stays
"enabling the registry plugin also installed the unconsented dependency: {installed:?}");

rationale:
A `use` name resolving to a registry plugin yields an identity whose `pm` is the registry's name (e.g. `user-plugins`), not `cargo`.

- `enabled_dependencies` dependency loop: `is_used` compares that id with `pms.identity(dep)` (pm `cargo`), so it is false; the dependency is enabled only by its own `auto-enable`. The second loop skips any id equal to a registry plugin's identity (`registry.iter().any(|p| pms.identity(&p.canonical) == id)`).
- `decide`: `used.contains(&pms.identity(id))` is false for the cargo id, so the offer stays a `Candidate`.

Tests (all pass): `discovery::tests::use_naming_a_registry_plugin_leaves_the_dependency_undecided` (`active` empty, one candidate); `tests/enablement.rs` `choosing_registry_plugin_does_not_enable_same_named_dependency` (no `a-guidance` skill installed after `use crate-a`).

**Refuted on review:** the argument assumes a registry plugin's identity never has `pm` = `cargo`, but `[[registry]] name` is free-form: `RawConfig::validate` passes `registries` through unchecked and `registry_instance` names the `PmInstance` after `cfg.name`, so a registry can be named `cargo`. Its plugins then get canonical ids with `pm` `cargo`; `PmRegistry::owner` matches by name and finds the cargo transport first, so `identity` folds them with cargo's rule. `identify` resolves `use = ["crate-a"]` to the registry plugin (registry-first) yet returns `cargo/crate_a`, the dependency's own identity. `enabled_dependencies` then sets `is_used` for the dependency, and `decide` classifies its offer `Used`. Reproduced with the prebuilt binary on the `auto-enable0` fixture plus a dormant registry entry `reg/crate-a/Symposium.toml` (`name = "crate-a"`): with the registry named `myreg`, `status` shows the dependency awaiting consent and `sync` installs nothing; with it named `cargo`, `status` shows `crate-a 0.1.0 — [plugins] use` and `sync` installs `.claude/skills/a-guidance/SKILL.md` from the unconsented dependency. So a `use` entry that resolves to a registry plugin does count as consent for the same-named dependency's embedded plugin whenever the registry is named `cargo`.
requirement: A `[plugins] use` entry that resolves to a registry plugin MUST NOT count as consent for the plugin embedded in a same-named dependency.
